title: Half-baked eval and rollout hypotheses - Clara Nguyen
content:
Context: quick late-night reaction to interview loop for Runtime Engineer candidate (senior). Not polished; dumping heuristics + potential follow-ups for panel.

High level impression: thoughtful engineer, strong systems grounding, weaker on tradeoff storytelling. Good instinctual mental model for batching/kv-cache but had trouble relating it to rollout guardrails and product constraints.

Quick score (out of 10):
- System design: 8
- Runtime/ops intuition: 8
- Product/roadmap thinking: 5
- Communication & async writeups: 6

What I liked (specific):
- Walked through a continuous-batching story from request distribution -> queue design -> backpressure mechanisms. Mentioned leaky-bucket style token accounting; practical.
- Knew the failure modes for KV cache staleness and described a lightweight invalidation approach using sequence stamps rather than full cache flushes.
- Comfortable describing kernel/quantization tradeoffs at a high level (FP16 vs int8 flow) and latency impacts for short vs long sequences.

Concerns / red flags (specific):
- When asked about rollout strategy for a new model that regresses on hallucination, default answer was "roll back" without proposing canary thresholds, metric gating, or offline eval sets — suggests ops-first reflex, less product nuance.
- Struggled to connect batching policy to multi-tenant cost allocation. Couldn't sketch a fair per-customer cost model or how to attribute cache hits to customers in shared pools.
- Async followup writing was terse in the take-home summary; diagrams missing, which makes me worry about cross-team handoffs.

Edge-case notes (interesting / unique):
- Proposed an optimization where prefix cache keys include a hashed client feature fingerprint to keep personalization while maintaining prefix reuse. Smart idea but complexity tradeoffs not fully explored (privacy, key explosion).
- Brought up ephemeral GPUs for burst capacity but assumed instant warm start. Needs more realism around cold KV warming and warm-up token storm mitigation.

Suggested interview/assignment follow-ups if we want them:
1) Short take-home: sketch a rollout plan for a model update that improves summary quality but increases hallucination for legal-doc workload. Ask for metric gating, canary size, user-facing mitigation, and rollback criteria. Evaluate for product thinking.
2) Pairing task (1hr): pair on instrumenting a simple in-memory prefix cache to show attribution of hits to tenants and design an eviction policy that balances fairness and throughput. Look for concrete tradeoffs and communication.
3) Written prompt: ask candidate to draft three concise alerting thresholds we'd put on a new model deployment and why. See clarity.

My suggested disposition: proceed to an additional take-home or informal pairing (medium). Candidate is strong technically and will add value to runtime team, but we need evidence of product/rollout thinking and clearer cross-team communication.

Potential fit and role framing notes for hiring doc:
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (not necessarily architect) — pragmatist, will move us forward on batching, cache and kernel-selection improvements.
- Growth areas to coach: product-minded rollout design, writing crisp runbooks and pre-mortems, quantifying cost attribution.
- Signals to look for in next interaction: concrete canary gating rules, a traced example of attribution math, a compact diagram or table in the writeup.

Followups for panel:
- Marco: ask about attribution math and multi-tenant cost allocation (5–10 min deep dive).
- Aisha: run pairing on prefix cache attribution with tenant keys (schedule 1hr).
- Me (Clara): request short written take-home described above; evaluate clarity and depth.

Loose hypotheses (half-baked):
- If the candidate can produce a short, structured rollout plan, they are likely a good hire for senior runtime role.
- If they cannot produce metric gating specifics, they are better suited to a deep infra individual contributor role with limited cross-product responsibility.

Misc notes to self:
- Make explicit in hiring rubric where we require product-thinking vs pure infra skill. Current rubric too weighted to microbenchmarks; want to add a 'rollout & gating' axis.
- Consider converting the pairing task into a 45 minute whiteboard + 30 minute writeup so we can evaluate both live reasoning and follow-up documentation.

Unresolved questions / things to capture in panel doc:
- Did any other interviewer see evasion of privacy concerns with hashed client fingerprint idea? If yes, capture pros/cons.
- Concrete examples of their past rollouts (URLs to PRs or postmortems) — I asked but didn't get links. Ask for them in followup.

End of dump. Will tidy if panel asks for formal feedback.
